newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-PONTING PUT ON STANDBY FOR FIRST ONE-DAY INTERNATIONAL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PONTING PUT ON STANDBY FOR FIRST ONE-DAY INTERNATIONAL.

text.p: Tasmanian Ricky Ponting has been put on standby for Thursday's first one-day international between England and Australia at Headingley after a knee injury to all-rounder Greg Blewett.
Ponting's ability as a change bowler will give him a place at number five in the order ahead of reserve wicketkeeper Adam Gilchrist if Blewett is unfit.
Michael Kasprowicz is likely to get the third pace bowler's place ahead of Andy Bichel, who was due to play his first match of the tour against Durham on Tuesday.
The match was abandoned after heavy overnight rain and Bichel, who had been suffering from a back strain, missed the chance to press for a place in the Australian side.
Australia, who started the tour late in order to give their players a break after the demands of their South African tour, have been hampered by some inclement if not untypical May weather.
They have played only two competitive matches, both of them one-dayers, and have only two three-day matches after the three-match one-day series before beginning their Ashes defence.
Australia, who set the pace in the one-day game during the 1980s, have fallen behind recently and this year failed for the first time to reach the finals of the World Series Cup.
"I've been criticised at times for playing down the one-dayers," Australian captain Mark Taylor conceded.
"I play the one-dayers as everyone does. We take them very seriously but they are drifting a long way from the test matches.
"It would be nice to win them because I think the side that does well will take some sort of psychological advantage from it come first test time, especially if it is won by either side."
England will probably omit teenage all-rounder Ben Hollioake, reserve spinner Ashley Giles and medium-fast Chris Silverwood.
They have gambled with the form of opener Nick Knight, who has played little cricket after breaking a finger in New Zealand during the winter tour.
England - Mike Atherton (captain), Nick Knight, Alec Stewart, Graham Thorpe, John Crawley, Graham Lloyd, Adam Hollioake, Phil DeFreitas, Darren Gough, Dean Headley, Robert Croft.
Australia - Mark Taylor (captain), Mark Waugh, Steve Waugh, Michael Bevan, Greg Blewett or Ricky Ponting, Michael Slater, Ian Healy, Shane Warne, Michael Kasprowicz, Jason Gillespie, Glenn McGrath.
